extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / news consumers (readers of AP wire historic coverage)
extracted.subtask_description: Wire-service news coverage of wartime and postwar events (trials, executions, government actions) including factual reporting and descriptions of legal/procedural developments at international military tribunals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of affidavits as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The tribunal ruled that affidavits may be admitted as evidence and pointed out that defense counsel could call the witnesses themselves if they wished cross‑examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense counsel objected that witnesses should appear in person and be cross‑examined; prosecutors (U.S., British, French, Soviet) opposed barring affidavits, arguing live testimony would unduly protract the trial. The tribunal balanced the need for expedition against the defense's right to cross‑examination by allowing affidavits but preserving defense ability to summon witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of captured German documents and SS reports as evidentiary material
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecutors read and submitted captured German documents and SS leather‑bound volumes showing reports of operations (e.g., Warsaw ghetto operations, extermination-camp reports) as part of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such documentary evidence was presented to provide detailed, contemporaneous accounts (burnings, deportations, gassing) and was described as having a clarity often unmatched by other accounts; documentary reports were used to establish scope and methods of extermination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of organizational guilt alongside individual trials
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosecution intended to devote remaining trial time to evidence against the Reich Cabinet, Nazi Party leadership corps, the S.S., Gestapo, S.A., and the high command general staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The United States considered determination of the guilt of Nazi organizations as fully as important as trials of individual leaders; U.S. participation in organizational determinations was justified as a means to reach thousands of lesser but culpable individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing full presentation of evidence with procedural efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice Robert H. Jackson insisted on the right to present all evidence before defense arguments are presented, while prosecutors warned that calling live witnesses for every affidavit could unduly prolong proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribunal decisions reflect a balancing test: allow comprehensive evidentiary presentation while avoiding undue prolongation; where affidavits are admitted, the defense retains the option to call witnesses for cross‑examination if they choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution of military court sentences after appeals process
rubrics_metrics.description: Death sentences pronounced by a British military court were carried out after appeals were denied (e.g., the eleven Belsen/Oswiecim convicts were executed after Marshal Montgomery denied all appeals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report presents the procedural fact that military‑court death sentences may be executed when appeals are exhausted or denied; timing and implementation (moving prisoners, erecting gallows, official announcements) follow military and judicial orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits to present statistical or high‑level estimates when direct testimony is impractical
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits (for example Dr. Wilhelm Hoettl's) were used to present large‑scale estimates such as numbers killed (e.g., attribution of 'six million' figure) when those estimates derived from internal SS sources and could not be presented solely by live witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits can convey organizational estimates or summaries compiled from internal records; their use allows the tribunal to consider aggregated statistical evidence while preserving defense rights to challenge or summon sources.
